sample_unit: hospitals (clients) in eICU and MIMIC-IV EHR datasets

links.outcome: Fairness gaps (EOPP, EOD, DP) across racial groups for mortality prediction models
links.effect: Personalized FL EOD 27.4% (eICU) and 47.8% (MIMIC-IV); standard FL 26.2% and 42.0%; standalone 69.4% and 54.7%. Personalization worsened fairness at less biased hospitals.
links.quote: Our findings also show that while personalization can improve fairness for more biased hospitals (i.e., hospitals having larger fairness gaps in standalone training), it can exacerbate fairness issues for less biased ones.

unlisted_practices: Using federated learning versus standalone training to improve group fairness in EHR prediction
Personalized federated learning (Ditto) for handling data heterogeneity across hospitals

screen.reason: Empirical study on real EHR datasets (eICU, MIMIC-IV) assessing the impact of personalized federated learning on group fairness and bias across health centers.

primary.practice: personalized federated learning for fairness auditing
